rows.verdict: The ranking is truncated and is not an exact mathematical statement or evidence of current openness.

rows.primary_locator: Bourgade, Random band matrices (2018), equation (0.1), conjecture (0.2), section 2.2
rows.source_quote: For d = 2, it is conjectured that all states are localized with a localization length of order exp(W2)
rows.exact_scope: Real symmetric matrix on Lambda={1,...,N}^2 with periodic L1 distance; centered entries independent up to symmetry; H_ij=0 beyond W; comparable variances of nonzero entries with each row variance sum one; section 2.2 adds uniform subgaussian tails for W H_ij. Bulk means |E|<2-kappa in the transition discussion. Conjecture (0.2) predicts W_c(N) of order sqrt(log N); section 2.2 predicts localization length of order exp(W^2). Poisson versus GOE is part of the transition expectation, not an established fixed-W theorem.
rows.correction: The intake writes this as an all-bulk-eigenvector and Poisson joint assertion at fixed W. The primary survey gives a heuristic scale and transition, without quantified finite-volume localization or a precise point-process convergence theorem for fixed W. Treat those as separate proof obligations.

rows.result: Lai-Yang v2 (2026-10-06) proves bulk delocalization when W >= (log N)^55 for the stated Gaussian two-dimensional torus model, yielding a stretched-exponential lower bound on localization length. It does not address fixed W as N tends to infinity.
